tips.title: Thinning Vallejo Model Air vs Model Color for Airbrushing
tips.text: For Vallejo Model Air, mix 1:1 paint to thinner using Vallejo Airbrush Thinner. For Model Color, mix 1:2 paint to thinner due to its thicker consistency. Add 2-3 drops of Vallejo Flow Improver per 10 drops of thinned paint for both. Spray Model Air at 1.2-1.8 bar, Model Color at 1.8-2.2 bar pressure.

tips.title: Base Coat Technique with Tamiya Spray Cans
tips.text: For base coats, use Tamiya Spray Cans. Shake well before use and apply in thin, even coats. Hold the can 12-18 inches away from the model. Apply 2-3 light coats, allowing 5-10 minutes drying time between coats. For darker colors, consider 4-5 light coats to avoid over-spray.

tips.title: Camouflage Masking with Eduard Masks
tips.text: Use Eduard Masks for complex camouflage schemes. Apply the masks while the paint is still wet for better adhesion. Peel off masks after the paint has dried for at least 24 hours. Apply a light coat of acrylic paint (e.g., Vallejo Model Color) along the mask edges to help prevent paint from bleeding under the masks.

tips.title: Applying AK Interactive Washes for Realistic Weathering
tips.text: Apply AK Interactive Washes using a soft, natural bristle brush. Work the wash into panel lines and other recesses. Remove excess wash with a dry brush or cotton swab after 10-15 minutes. For a more subtle effect, use a mix of AK Interactive Washes and AK Interactive Thinner (1:1 ratio).

tips.title: Chipping Technique with Mr. Hobby Chipping Colors
tips.text: For chipping effects, use Mr. Hobby Chipping Colors. Apply the color where chips are desired using a fine brush. Allow to dry, then gently dab the areas with a sponge dampened with water and a drop of dish soap. For a more pronounced effect, use a stiff brush to lightly scrub the area before applying the chipping color.
